rationale_summary: Colorado SB 24-205 is dominantly framed around fundamental rights, centering its entire regulatory duty of reasonable care on preventing unlawful algorithmic discrimination across protected civil-rights characteristics while guaranteeing individual profiling opt-out rights, personal-data correction, accessible explanations, human appeal review of adverse consequential decisions, and explicit federal and state constitutional free-speech safeguards. Consumer and public safety serves as a closely intertwined secondary frame: the statute is titled as a consumer-protection act, codified directly into the Colorado Consumer Protection Act's unfair and deceptive trade practice provisions, mandates clear AI interaction notices for consumers, preserves emergency life-and-safety actions and product recalls, and invokes the General Assembly's public-health-and-safety clause. Innovation enablement acts as a measured third frame through small-deployer carve-outs, pre-market research and testing exclusions, trade-secret confidentiality, and NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001 compliance safe harbors.
